title: Probative Embedding Accuracy Harness & Load Probe
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Deliver a repeatable evaluation harness that measures embedding accuracy across curated reference corpora, produces offline quality metrics for reranking, and includes a load probe to validate latency/throughput regressions under increasing QPS. The harness must integrate with nightly CI, surface drift signals to Console, and provide artifacted golden reference sets for reproducible comparisons.

Scope and components:
- Reference corpora: curate three domain slices (docs, conversational, short-form Q&A) with explicit positive/negative relevance judgments and deterministic seed splits. These are the canonical 'reference sets' used for accuracy computation.
- Offline metrics: implement nDCG@k, MRR, recall@k, pairwise AUC, and cosine-distance calibration statistics. Export per-query and aggregated histograms to telemetry.
- Drift monitoring: nightly job that compares current model embeddings to the baseline reference epoch using distributional tests (KS on cosine distributions, centroid drift, nearest-neighbor stability) and thresholded alerts.
- Scalability probe: synthetic traffic generator that replays representative request shapes to rerank endpoint at 10, 50, 100, and 250 QPS. Measure p50/p90/p95 token latency, end-to-end rerank latency, memory/KV cache hit rates, and failure modes.
- CI & artifacting: results + metrics must be stored in S3 with semantic naming (model_version/commit/timestamp) and a human-readable HTML report linked in the nightly pipeline.
- Observability integration: add telemetry to Console dashboards for per-model embedding drift score, nightly delta, and rolling 7-day trend. Open an alert if drift_score > 0.12 AND nDCG@10 drops by >= 3%.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Nightly job runs in CI and uploads artifacts for all three slices (pass/fail and metrics).
2) Scalability probe produces repeatable load-tests with published baseline numbers for p95 latency under 100 QPS.
3) Drift alerts are emitted to PagerDuty (devops channel) when threshold hit and a corresponding Console card shows historical context.
4) A PR with end-to-end test coverage and clear runbook for false-positive handling is merged.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not include automatic retraining or model rollback flows (those are follow-ups).
- It does not change production model selection policies; it only produces signals and artifacts for decision-making.
updates: 2026-02-06: Initial spike completed. Identified three domain slices and drafted schema for relevance judgments. Confluence doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Probative+Embedding+Harness
2026-02-18: Design review with PM/Research. Decided on KS-test + centroid-shift metrics for drift. Action: add normalization step (L2) to eliminate scale differences.

2026-02-25: Prototype offline runner implemented (python) and ran against model v1.13. Observed nDCG@10 baseline: docs 0.67, convo 0.61, short-form 0.72. Telemetry export format v1 drafted. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/eval-harness/pull/142

2026-03-03: Scalability probe PoC executed in staging. 100 QPS stress resulted in p95 end-to-end rerank latency 182ms, KV cache hit 84%. Memory pressure reproduced on certain model shards. Filed ENG-93579 for memory tuning.

2026-03-09: Nightly job wired into CI (pipeline: nightly/embedding-eval). Artifacts land in s3://redwood-eval/embeddings/{model}/{date}. HTML report template attached to PR. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ci/pull/210

2026-03-12: Dashboard prototype on Console shows per-model drift score + seven-day delta. Alerting rules staged but not yet routing to PagerDuty. Next: finalize thresholds and run two-week bake period before enabling paging.
notes: Trade-offs considered: heavy-weight human-curated golden sets improve signal but increase maintenance cost; mitigated by automated augmentation + periodic steward review.
Decision: keep three domain slices to balance signal granularity and operational cost. Can add vertical-specific slices later if customers request.
Operational risk: false-positive drift alerts. Mitigation: composite rule requiring both distributional drift and a concrete metric drop (nDCG) before triggering PagerDuty.
